scope: Local Windows playtest and repair of desktop camera response and HUD scale.
owner_finding: I can't turn the camera at all hardly.

camera.method: In each rendered Windows package, the test queried Slate's real hit-test grid, delivered synthetic pointer events directly to the chosen widget, inspected capture/release replies and read the active pawn camera. The bridge start used the bridge fixture. No physical mouse was injected.
verified: Relative capture requested for left and right buttons
Stationary screen position plus 240 horizontal raw counts produced 90 degrees of camera yaw
Eight opposite 30-count samples restored the starting angle
20 raw counts upward produced 6 degrees of upward tilt
Exterior orbit radius and bridge eye distance held
Open space hit the camera and a command button remained reachable above it
Release requested cursor restoration; motion after release or capture loss was ignored
Looking while paused worked in both views
A 0.1-second release held the view; after 3 seconds exterior returned behind the ship and bridge kept its heading
camera.report_output: The packaged test exporter wrote both JSON results. Its optional HTML template was absent.

hud.measurement: Maximum uninterrupted vertical run of enabled expedition button fill RGB (2,8,9) within the top-right command area. Borders excluded.

playtest.exit: Window closed normally with status zero

prior_package_keyboard_check: The earlier Windows binary received E through Unreal Enhanced Input. The separate test save entered outbound travel; this was not a human order.
limits: Comfort with a physical mouse on the corrected build and full expedition pacing await the owner.
The Windows UI automation pipe was unavailable. Packaged camera checks covered widget hit testing, pointer handling, and camera transforms.
Android, sustained phone performance, cloud saves and Apple were not exercised in this Windows pass.
